slides.title: Google DeepMind - Griffin & Hawk https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19427 -
slides.text: Google DeepMind - Griffin & Hawk https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19427 - paper Hawk and Griffin are new RNNs by DeepMind . Hawk  - high performance (faster than Mamba) using gated linear recurrences Griffin - matches Llama-2’s performance with significantly less training data . Griffin is a hybrid combining gated linear recurrences and local attention. Griffin - handles long sequences (longer than seen during training). Both models are as hardware efficient as Transformers, but offer lower latency and higher throughput during inference. Griffin is scaled to 14 billion parameters. https://artgor.medium.com/paper-review-griffin-mixing-gated-linear-recurrences-with-local-attention-for-efficient-language-75e5a86b1b24 https://medium.com/@bnjmn_marie/griffin-and-hawk-local-attention-for-efficient-language-models-7856fbb6bb32 Griffin & Hawk

slides.title: One problem with RAG is that the questions
slides.text: One problem with RAG is that the questions and answers don't have to be semantically similar. One way of solving it is to do the search in the space of questions. Text vector indexing: split text into text chunks, generate embedding vectors from those text chunks , index them as (vector_from_text, text) Question vector indexing: split text into big chunks - chapters. for each chapter generate multiple "exam" questions generate embedding vectors from questions index them as (vector_from_question, text) You can also use hybrid approach using both methods together Make RAG Better LLM Agent Classifier, may ask to refine question LLM Agent question rewriter, embedding LLM Agent semantic re-runking LLM Agent summarizer Response Request Semantic re-runking: You send question and the chunk of text to LLM - and ask it to rank the relevancy of the text to the question. If your search found 10 text chunks - you can make 10 separate queries to LLM, get 10 ranks - and sort them to select the best match. You can make those 10 queries in parallel (for speed). Any good LLM can be used (Mixtral, for example). You can program agents using LangChain or LlamaIndex Some good techniques to use: classification step query expansion re-ranking prompt engineering tool use

slides.title: Ollama supports embedding models https://ollama.com/blog/embedding-models for example: mxbai-embed-large
slides.text: Ollama supports embedding models https://ollama.com/blog/embedding-models for example: mxbai-embed-large (334M parameters) nomic-embed-text (137M parameters) all-minilm (23M parameters) So you can use Ollama for RAG (both embedding and LLM) Ollama & Embedding Models # ollama pull mxbai-embed-large ## REST API curl http://localhost:11434/api/embeddings -d '{ "model": "mxbai-embed-large", "prompt": "some text to convert" }' ## Python Library ollama.embeddings( model='mxbai-embed-large', prompt='some text to convert', ) ## JavaScript Library ollama.embeddings({ model: 'mxbai-embed-large', prompt: 'some text to convert', })

slides.title: AIOS = AI OS (AI Operating System) open
slides.text: AIOS = AI OS (AI Operating System) open source LLM Agent operating system embeds large language model into Operating Systems (OS) as the brain of the OS enables an operating system "with soul" It is an important step towards AGI. AIOS is designed to: optimize resource allocation, facilitate context switch across agents, enable concurrent execution of agents, provide tool service for agents, maintain access control for agents, provide a rich set of toolkits for developers https://github.com/agiresearch/AIOS AIOS: LLM Agent Operating System
